question: Are the length-scaled motion/momentum notation and additive contact matrices new?
assessment: Length scaling itself is not unique: explicit planar velocity/torque dual scaling is in RSS2011. The exact momentum symbol arrangement was not located, but follows directly from established dual scaling. No research contribution or priority established solely by notation.

sources.author: Roy Featherstone
sources.title: General Comments on Coordinate Transforms
sources.supports: Spatial motion/force duality and dual inertia transforms.

sources.authors: Kevin M. Lynch and Frank C. Park
sources.title: Modern Robotics, 3.4 Wrenches

sources.author: Jorge Angeles
sources.title: On the Optimum Dimensioning of Robotic Manipulators
sources.supports: Sections1-2 establish prior characteristic-length normalization for mixed-dimensional Jacobians. This is not a claim of the identical contact notation.

sources.authors: Thomas H. Vose, Paul Umbanhowar, Kevin M. Lynch
sources.title: Sliding Manipulation of Rigid Bodies on a Controlled 6-DoF Plate
sources.verification: Full proceedings PDF downloaded and converted with pdftotext; equation text examined.
sources.supports: Direct planar velocity scaled by radius of gyration and torque divided by the same length.
sources.difference: Force/torque rather than momentum; radius of gyration rather than arbitrary fixed ell.

sources.authors: Ying Zhang, Hai-Jun Su, Qizheng Liao
sources.title: Mobility criteria of compliant mechanisms based on decomposition of compliance matrices
sources.verification: Publisher metadata and author-uploaded manuscript full text examined.
sources.supports: Explicit scaling of rotation by characteristic length and moment by reciprocal length.
sources.difference: Rotation-first small-deformation twist and applied moment, not literally our velocity/momentum vectors.

sources.title: A New Algebraic Rigid-Body Collision Law Based on Impulse Space Considerations
sources.location: Abstract and sections3-6 of original manuscript
sources.verification: Original-paper text examined via manuscript rendering; publisher DOI fetch failed.
sources.supports: 3D frictional point collisions with two restitution parameters and admissible impulse/energy region.
sources.difference: Its impulse-selection rule and sequential multiple-impact treatment are not asserted identical to our simultaneous endpoint model.

sources.title: On the Moreau–Jean scheme with the Frémond impact law: energy conservation and dissipation properties for elastodynamics with contact, impact and friction
sources.verification: Publisher full PDF read in browser and downloaded/converted.
sources.supports: General Moreau normal/tangential restitution with friction, Delassus coupling and limitations of dissipation guarantees.
sources.difference: No claim their thermodynamically motivated law, local admissibility or integration scheme equals our endpoint acceptance gate.

sources.title: Contact and Friction Simulation for Computer Graphics
sources.location: Figure43 and matrix-free tutorial, PDF pages163-164
sources.verification: Full course PDF examined through browser.
sources.difference: General operation organization is prior art; does not settle novelty of every production solver detail.

sources.authors: Nima Fazeli, Samuel Zapolsky, Evan Drumwright, Alberto Rodriguez
sources.title: Fundamental Limitations in Performance and Interpretability of Common Planar Rigid-Body Contact Models
sources.location: Abstract; empirical comparison and parameter-interpretation discussion
sources.verification: Author preprint downloaded and converted; primary arXiv record checked.
sources.supports: Comparison of six impact models and difficulty interpreting fitted parameters.
sources.difference: Our proposed fixed independently characterized input test differs from fitting against comparison outcomes; no first-ever claim for such tests.

choices_in_this_article: Signed lever R=[-r/ell]_cross yielding additive contact velocity
Consistent 2D/3D dual impulse, mass, restitution, friction capacity and matrix-free coupling
mathematical_status: D=diag(I,ell*I) is invertible; momentum uses D^-T, mass uses D^-T M0 D^-1 and contact map uses C0 D^-1; physical Delassus response unchanged.
limitations: Limited primary-source review, not an exhaustive priority search.
No evidence established that the exact symbol arrangement is first in the literature.
Notation scaling does not introduce or validate a new constitutive contact law.
